Family Health Nursing

The family as the unit of care — family assessment, family life cycle, roles and family health nursing process.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the family as a unit of care
  • List the stages of the family life cycle
  • Perform a family assessment
  • Apply the nursing process to a family

In simple words

The family, not the individual, is the basic unit of health care. Illness of one member affects the whole family, and care works best when the whole family is involved.

Family types

  • Nuclear family — husband, wife and children
  • Joint family — relatives living together with common kitchen
  • Extended family — nuclear family plus other relatives
  • Single parent / blended / childless — other accepted forms

Stages of the family life cycle

  1. Marriage (family formation)
  2. Childbearing — births in the first years
  3. Child rearing — school age and adolescence
  4. Launching — children leave home, marriage
  5. Empty nest to retirement
  6. Aging and death

Family assessment

Domain What to record
Structure Members, ages, education, occupation, married status
Housing Rooms, ventilation, water source, animals, overcrowding
Health Illness, disability, food, medicines, screening due
Roles and relationships Decision-making, communication, support
Resources Income, assets, food availability, transport
Health behaviour Cleanliness, food habits, harmful habits
Problems identified Ranked by priority

Family health nursing process

  1. Assess the family as a whole
  2. Identify and rank health problems
  3. Plan care with the family — the family decides
  4. Implement: teach, treat, refer, mobilise resources
  5. Evaluate and follow up; record in the family folder

🔴 Care for the whole family

If the mother has anaemia, treat the whole family’s food habits; if a child is malnourished, teach the family, not just the mother. The family is the unit of both illness and care.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. The family is the basic unit of health care.
  2. Family types: nuclear, joint, extended, single parent.
  3. Life cycle stages: formation, childbearing, rearing, launching, ageing.
  4. Assessment covers structure, housing, health, roles, resources.
  5. Plan care with the family, not for the family.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Overcrowding increases respiratory and skin disease.
  2. Decision-making style guides how teaching is planned.
  3. Roles change during illness when the earner becomes dependent.
  4. The family folder gives continuity of care at each visit.
  5. Rank problems with the family so that priorities are accepted.

📌 Memory trick

Family life cycle: M-F-R-L-A — Marriage, Fertility, Rearing, Launching, Ageing.

60-second revision

  • Family, not the individual, is the unit of care.
  • Types: nuclear, joint, extended, single parent.
  • Six life cycle stages from marriage to ageing.
  • Assess structure, housing, health, roles, resources.
  • Nursing process applied to the family with its participation.

Test yourself

The basic unit of community health nursing is the:

Answer: B. The family is the basic unit of care since illness and health behaviour are shared by all its members.

Which is a joint family feature?

Answer: B. In a joint family, relatives of more than one generation live together sharing a common kitchen.

The stage of launching in the family life cycle is when:

Answer: B. Launching is the stage when children mature, marry and leave the parental home.

Family assessment includes:

Answer: B. Assessment covers family structure, housing, health, roles, resources and health behaviour.

Family care plan should be:

Answer: B. The plan is made with the family, so the priorities and actions are acceptable and achievable.
